transport.qualification: Required target profiles, not proven support. Qualify both handshakes, metadata and errors with the pinned SDK in T-06 and actual clients in T-14.
transport.authentication: Dedicated purpose/resource-bound MCP bearer on every request; no web-cookie, Google bearer or API-key fallback

profiles.subsequent_metadata: MCP-Protocol-Version header, authorization bearer on every HTTP request
Complete io.modelcontextprotocol protocol-version and client-capabilities metadata in params._meta; body is authoritative and mirrored headers must agree
profiles.discovery: server/discover implemented by server; optional client discovery; no modern initialize handshake

authorization.account_source: Current token and grant; never caller arguments, session preference or cursor claims
authorization.effective_scopes: Intersection of token ceiling, grant ceiling and live membership permissions
authorization.revalidation: Every discovery/call/replay; again under account mutex at mutation authorization
authorization.discovery: Only tools whose minimum scopes are presently allowed; optional projections and arguments independently checked
authorization.conditional_scope_failure: Reject explicitly requested unauthorized projection or input; do not silently omit protected data
authorization.empty_scope: connection_info only; client setup must request a useful explicit preset or qualify actual step-up

roles.admin: All declared Permissions scopes, intersected with token and grant ceilings
roles.read-only: Only declared scopes ending in .read; no mutation by write/send permission
roles.restricted: Only explicit current membership scopes, intersected with token and grant ceilings
roles.unknown_or_absent: Deny before tool discovery or invocation

authorization.mutation_lock_order: Account -> current membership -> client -> grant -> bearer token -> operation source; all revocation/membership mutation paths use the same account-first boundary, never invert it for last_used_at
authorization.token_user_type: Local User only; account API keys and Google identity tokens are different credential purposes

wire_limits.request_policy: Bound raw envelope first, reject duplicate decoded members and invalid exact integer lexemes before native JSON decode; separately retain T17 semantic/wire message budgets
wire_limits.result_policy: Count complete actual serialized RPC envelope including mirrored TextContent and structuredContent; byte-aware page cuts preserve ordering and continuation
wire_limits.single_item_too_large: result_too_large; never silently truncate content or return a non-advancing cursor
wire_limits.post_commit_failure: Safe error with applied/unknown outcome and owned reference if known; mail_send retries same key/payload only

admission.storage: SQL atomic windows; apply all relevant dimensions before side effects
admission.ip_key: HMAC-SHA256 of normalized trusted peer IP and UTC day, using purpose-separated application key
admission.trusted_proxy_policy: Only explicitly configured proxies; never trust arbitrary forwarded IP headers
admission.business_quotas: Existing common account sending quotas remain additional limits; transport limits do not authorize mail
admission.retry_after: Ceiling seconds to the latest exhausted window; HTTP429 before invocation, no business effect

retention.preregistered_client_expiry: Explicit operator revocation; no idle expiration
retention.accepted_source_exception: Preserve immutable receipt and provenance tombstones while accepted work refers to them; no cascading loss of accepted work
retention.cleanup: Bounded finite command, scheduled through existing scheduler; expire/revoke atomically before deletion, preserve active work and source references

cursor.encryption_proposal: Laravel encryptString/decryptString using configured application encrypter and trusted previous-key ring; no serialize/unserialize or custom cipher.
cursor.wire_encoding: Replace standard base64 +/ with -_, remove trailing =; strict canonical reverse before framework authenticated decryption.
policy: Current bearer/grant/account/membership/projection authorization runs before cursor processing and again before reading; cookies/API keys/Google tokens cannot authenticate MCP.
Authenticate the framework ciphertext before interpreting payload fields; the model proof assumes decryption already verified and does not prove encryption.
Use exact trusted resource URI hash and explicit account/user/grant identities, never request Host or a cursor-supplied identity.
authorization_hash is a server-canonical hash of current effective scopes and grant authorization revision; role/scope changes invalidate the old cursor even when a read remains permitted.
filter_hash covers effective domain filters and owned parent identifiers; clients repeat filters on continuation, not merely the cursor.
For default activity dates, carry the resolved date window in the authenticated cursor and reuse it on continuation; crossing midnight does not silently change the query.
Hash filters after common-service normalization. Never independently trim/change search semantics or echo filter hashes as evidence of authorization.
Fingerprints use sorted object keys and validated domain primitives, never raw numeric tokens or client-provided hashes; exact ID decimals stay strings without float/int overflow.
Bind only the paged subprojection, not unrelated optional static projections or page size; every separately requested projection still requires current scopes.
campaigns_review recipient continuation targets campaigns_get with include.recipients, not campaigns_review; no second revision is created to continue a page.
Campaign recipient cursors bind campaign/reviewed revision; a changed revision yields version_conflict, never mixed snapshots or a silent page-one fallback.
imports_get binds the owned report id and orders row_number ascending; campaign recipients order id ascending; standard lists and attempts order id descending.
Activity ordering is occurred_at descending then opaque record_key descending; use bound SQL tuple predicates on the shared query, not OFFSET or numeric parsing of record_key.
Lifetime is at most 900 seconds and never exceeds the authenticated access token expiry; require expires_at>issued_at and reject issuance more than 30 seconds in the future.
Invalid ciphertext, malformed payload or cross-context cursor maps to cursor_invalid; exact expiry maps to cursor_expired after valid binding; never log raw cursor or plaintext.
Key rotation uses only trusted configured current/previous keys; removing a previous key may invalidate cursors and requires a fresh query, never a plaintext fallback.
Read at most limit+1 ordered candidates, build the full serialized MCP result including both text and structuredContent and the actual continuation cursor.
If the wire cap cuts a page early, retain all unreturned rows through a cursor after the last emitted row. No dropped rows, empty has_more=true page or false terminal page.
If static output plus the first item cannot fit, return result_too_large with actionable safe recovery; never truncate content or mutate resources during a read.
If result construction fails after a committed review, return the approved applied-outcome error with an owned revision reference; inspect it rather than review again.
Ordinary activity pages are a live SQL view, not a fixed cross-page transaction snapshot; campaign recipient pages remain bound to an immutable revision.

key_lifecycle.opaque_access_tokens: High-entropy Sanctum plaintext returned only once, SHA-256 hash persisted; no JWT signature/public JWKS invented
key_lifecycle.authorization_code: Cryptographic random code, hash only, 300 seconds, one atomic consumption; replay invalidates tokens from that code without disclosing token values
key_lifecycle.grant_reuse: No silent extension: each reauthorization creates a new consented grant with current membership/scopes; expired or revoked grants never become active again
key_lifecycle.application_key_rotation: Persist trusted current and previous Laravel encrypter keys; new cursors use current key, old cursors may decrypt only with configured previous keys. Keep previous key at least the 900-second cursor lifetime plus 30-second skew, then remove after expiry. Never accept cursor-provided keys.
key_lifecycle.emergency_rotation_or_restore: Atomically revoke all potentially compromised/restored MCP grants/tokens and pending codes, rotate private application/HMAC material, invalidate old cursor rings, then require new authorization; preserve immutable receipts/provenance
key_lifecycle.idempotency: Account namespace and canonical fingerprint never depend on APP_KEY, token, grant, client or transport; preserve T-17 receipts across rotation
